tierA_rule: Any token with a capital letter after the first, a digit, _ / . + or :: (identifiers, topics, files, commands), and everything inside backticks, stays exactly as in English. Frame names like map, odom, base_link stay English when they name a frame.

style: Readers are complete beginners and native Burmese readers. Write correct, plain, spoken Burmese (Myanmar Unicode only, never Zawgyi).
Body text: polite spoken register, endings ပါတယ် / ပါ / ပါမယ် / ပါဘူး / လား / သလဲ. Never literary forms: သည် ၏ ၌ ၍ သော ၎င်း; use နဲ့ not နှင့်, က not မှ (from), ကို not သို့.
role label/aria: short bare verb or noun, no sentence ending, no ။. role heading: short, no ။ unless the English is a full sentence.
Drop the pronoun where Burmese drops it; where needed use သင်.
Translate the instruction, not the words: natural Burmese order, short sentences, an idiom becomes its plain meaning, the simplest everyday word wins.
Keep tier A terms in Latin letters exactly; keep every identifier, topic, file name, command, number, unit and backtick span exactly as in the English. Western digits only.
Use the pinned tier B spellings, tier C words and UI verbs every time.
Punctuation: ၊ inside, ။ at the end of each Burmese sentence, never '.' after Burmese. Keep ':' '?' '→' '×' and arrows as in English. No zero-width spaces.
The Japanese (ja) is a second view of the meaning; translate from the English.
